method: Adversarial second pass over all 41 proposals (3 singular / 36 plural / 2 gender) — no sampling. Every 'to' was fetched fresh from svenska.se via dict-fetch (SAOL+SO+SAOB) rather than read from the first round's quotation; the first round's citations were treated as claims to be tested, not evidence. Beyond per-word lookup I ran six structural tests the first round could not run on itself: (1) FROM-VALUE TEST — reconstructed all 39 stored rows from REFERENCE TRANSLATIONS/image-vocabulary.js and confirmed every 'from' matches the live data (39/39 match; no proposal is arguing about a value that is not there). (2) RULE-7 DUP SCAN — patched all 39 rows and diffed each against all 1263 keys, distinguishing pre-existing duplicates from ones the fix CREATES; exactly one new collision surfaced (hospital-gown/scrubs), and it is escalated. (3) CROSS-LOCALE SHAPE TEST — read all 11 locales of each touched key; where Swedish alone diverges in shape (a mass noun where 10 locales have a countable pair) that is recorded, because it usually marks a lemma defect the form fix would entrench. (4) DIACRITIC/NFC TEST — programmatic check for the ASCII-folding defect that hit the earlier sv round ('Mikrovagsugn', 'Hav'): 0 defects; all five diacritic-bearing forms (Bärbara stereor, Byråar, Förgätmigejer, Trädgårdsgrepar, Sjukhuskläder) carry å/ä/ö correctly, and no proposal makes a naive repair of the ara→åra / hav→håv class. (5) PICTURE TEST — independently opened the images the verdicts actually turn on (cape, trapezoid, dresser, pegasus, garden_fork) rather than trusting image_seen. (6) BOTH-AUTHORITIES TEST — read the SO entry as well as the SAOL entry for every word, specifically hunting the brief's rule-5 SAOL/SO disagreement class; this is what produced the single REJECT. conflicts-sv.json is empty: nothing here reverses a shipped native decision.

rows.note: Verified independently. SAOL: 'kapa verb ~de ~t' — the stored singular is a VERB, and *Kapor is its script-invented plural. SAOL 'cape [kä´p] substantiv ~n [-en]; pl. ~r [-er] / ett ärmlöst plagg som läggs över axlarna'; SO 'cape capen caper / ett ärmlöst, jackliknande ytterplagg som hängs över axlarna'. I OPENED accessories/cape@2x.webp myself: a purple garment with a wide pointed shoulder collar and a button row, flaring to a hem, with NO sleeves of any kind — SAOL's definition word for word. The kappa-typo hypothesis is correctly rejected: a kappa has sleeves. I ALSO tested a trap the first round did not mention — da 'Kappe' and no 'Kappe' both sit in this same row, and Danish/Norwegian kappe DOES mean cloak/cape, which makes 'Kapa' look like a Scandinavian sibling form; but per §A.13.58 that must not be cross-applied — Swedish kappa is a COAT (sleeved), so the sibling evidence does not rescue the stored value, it is a false friend. MINOR PREMISE CORRECTION (does not touch the verdict): 'There is NO noun kapa' is overstated — SAOB lists a 'kapa sbst.' — but SAOL, the norm, carries only the verb, and no noun kapa means a cape.

Verified verbatim. SAOL returns 'Inga träffar på muffin. Menade du muffins, mufflon eller muff?' — quoted accurately, not fabricated. SAOL 'muffins [muf´ins] substantiv ~en hellre än ~et; pl. ~ hellre än ~ar'; SO 'muffins muffinsen, plural muffins el. muffinsar'. The Swedish borrowing took the English plural as its singular: en muffins. ROW COHERENCE (rule 7) CHECKED AND CLEAN: the resulting row is Muffins/Muffins/n — the plural field needs no change because SAOL PREFERS the zero plural ('pl. ~ hellre än ~ar'), and the gender needs no change because SAOL prefers ~en (= n). So the absence of a paired plural proposal is correct, not an oversight. Dup scan: no sister key collides. Cross-locale: no is already Muffins/Muffinser, so sv is not made an outlier.

SAOL 'pegas [pega´s] substantiv ~en ~er / bevingad häst som symbol för diktkonsten'; SO 'pegas pegasen pegaser'. SAOL carries no 'pegasus' headword. For a common-noun picture label, pegas is the naturalised Swedish word. PREMISE NUANCE the first round missed, recorded because the brief says a false premise must not be reused even when the conclusion is right: 'Pegasus' is not simply un-Swedish — SAOB explicitly states 'Ss. namn i obest. form användas numera bl. formerna pegasus o. pegasos', i.e. AS A PROPER NAME the form pegasus is the current one. That does not save the stored value here, because this row is a countable common-noun label in a picture vocabulary (and the corpus gives it hasPlural), not the name of the mythological horse. ART FINDING INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED: I opened Things That Fly/pegasus@2x.webp — the winged horse carries a GOLDEN SPIRAL HORN, so it is an alicorn/winged unicorn and is not a pegas in any language. That is a cross-locale art question for the operator; the form fix stands either way.

SAOL 'luft|kond·it·ion·er·ing substantiv ~en ~ar'; SO 'luftkonditionering luftkonditioneringen luftkonditioneringar'. Both authorities agree; the stored zero plural is unsupported. Agrees with classification hasPlural:true; the row's own _countable:false is the fallible field the brief warns about.
SAOL 'vrist substantiv ~en ~er'; SO 'vrist vristen vrister'. Both agree on -er. Textbook case of the documented -ar default swallowing the 3rd declension (ambulans/antilop/paj).

SAOL 'sparr·is [spar´-] substantiv ~en ~ar'; SO 'sparris sparrisen sparrisar'. Both agree. The brief itself names asparagus as a word whose _countable:false is wrong, and SAOL confirms the real plural.

SO 'baby babyn, plural babies el. babys' — babies first-listed. SAOL gives only '~n' and lists no plural at all. Checked specifically for the rule-5 SAOL/SO conflict class: this is NOT one — SAOL is SILENT, it does not offer a competing form, so SO governs unopposed. 'Babyar' appears in neither authority.

SAOL 'body [båd´y] substantiv ~n; pl. bodies'; SO 'body bodyn bodies'. Both agree, and the compound follows its head: babybody -> babybodies. noImage, so judged on the word alone, which is legitimate here because the fix is a pure declension of an attested head noun.
SAOL 'bagel [bej´gel] substantiv ~n; pl. ~s'; SO 'bagel bageln bagels'. Both agree on -s. 'Baglar' applies -el syncope (nyckel->nycklar) to an English loan SAOL does not syncopate.

Both halves verified. NOUN: SAOL '1stereo [ste´reo] substantiv ~n ~r / stereoanläggning' -> stereor, not *stereoar (note SAOL's 2stereo 'oböjl.' is stereofoni, the wrong homograph — the fix takes the right one). ADJECTIVE: an indefinite plural attributive takes -a -> bärbara. I VERIFIED THE CITED PRECEDENT IN THE LIVE DATA rather than taking it on trust: boiled-egg is ['Kokt ägg','Kokta ägg','t'] and fried-egg is ['Stekt ägg','Stekta ägg','t'] — the corpus already inflects the adjective in the plural in both sibling rows, which proves 'Bärbar stereoar' is a defect and not a house convention.

SAOL 'cape substantiv ~n [-en]; pl. ~r [-er]'; SO 'cape capen caper'. Both agree -> Caper. Moves coherently with the singular fix (rule 7): the row becomes Cape/Caper/n, a single consistent lemma, and the dup scan shows no sister-key collision.

SAOL 'chili|peppar substantiv ~n' — no plural listed; SO 'chilipeppar chilipepparn' — no plural listed. Also checked the short form: SAOL 'chili [çi´li] substantiv ~n', likewise none. I FOUND A STRONGER CONTROL THAN THE PROPOSAL'S: SAOL gives 'paprika [pa´prika] substantiv ~n paprikor' glossed 'krydda el. grönsak av en växt' — i.e. SAOL DOES grant a plural to a word that is simultaneously a spice AND a vegetable, in this very domain. Withholding one from chilipeppar is therefore a deliberate lexicographic choice, not an omission. The proposal's nyckel control only showed SAOL lists plurals in general; paprika shows it lists them for spice/vegetable homographs specifically. FLAG for the operator (not an objection): this key has NO image, so the classifier had nothing to see, and all 10 other locales use a countable POD word (de Chilischote/Chilischoten, fr Piment/Piments, es Chile/Chiles, it Peperoncino/Peperoncini, nl Chilipeper/Chilipepers) — the fix makes sv the only locale without a plural. The form fix is right against SAOL; the residual is a lemma question (chilifrukt/chilis), which is the operator's call.
SAOL 'korn·ell [-el´] substantiv ~en ~er'; SO 'kornell kornellen korneller'. Both agree. 'Kornellar' is the -ar default and does not exist.

STRONGEST CATCH IN THE SET AND IT SURVIVES ADVERSARIAL TESTING — this is the bok/böcker-vs-bokar homograph class the brief says is the worst thing to get wrong, and the first round got it right. I fetched the entry myself: SAOL '1byrå [by´rå] substantiv ~n ~ar / en möbel' and '2byrå [by´rå] substantiv ~n ~er / avdelning av ämbetsverk e.d.; kontor, mottagning; företag'; SO confirms '1 byrå byrån byråar / en (finare) förvaringsmöbel med utdragbara lådor' vs '2 byrå byrån byråer'. I OPENED furniture/dresser@2x.webp myself: a red-brown chest of four tan drawers with round knobs on splayed legs — unambiguously the FURNITURE, i.e. 1byrå -> byråar. The stored 'Byråer' is a real Swedish word (the office plural) bolted to the wrong sense, which is exactly why only the picture could settle it.
SAOL 'durian [du´-] substantiv ~en ~er / en stor, sydostasiatisk frukt'. SO has no entry ('Inga träffar på durian'), so SAOL governs unopposed — not a rule-5 conflict. 'Durianar' is the -ar default.

SAOL 'för·gät·mig|ej [-ej´] substantiv ~en; pl. ~ el. ~er'; SO 'plural förgätmigej el. förgätmigejer'. Confirmed: -ar is sanctioned by NEITHER authority, so the stored value must go, and BOTH zero and -er are sanctioned, so the chosen -er is not wrong. NOTED INCONSISTENCY, surfaced for the operator rather than treated as an error: this proposal takes SAOL's SECOND-listed form (-er) while the keyboard proposal in the same batch explicitly takes SAOL's FIRST-listed form ('Taking SAOL's first-listed form: Keyboardar'). Two different first-listed policies inside one batch. Both förgätmigej and förgätmigejer are correct, so I do not AMEND — but the operator should pick ONE policy, and the proposal's pedagogical rationale (a zero plural teaches nothing when read aloud beside a picture) is a reasonable basis for it. Independent of the singular, which is correctly HELD (the art is a large RED flower, not a small blue clustered förgätmigej).

CONFIRMED, AND I UPGRADE THE EVIDENCE — the proposal honestly flagged that it rested on sv.wiktionary plus a declension rule because 'SAOL's grep entry sits behind a six-way disambiguation page the fetch tool cannot resolve past'. That is true of the lemma search, but the authority CAN be reached from the other side: searching the INFLECTED form 'grepar' on svenska.se returns '2 träffar i SAOL, 2 träffar i SO' listing 'grepar (grep) subst.' and 'grepar (grepe) subst.' in BOTH dictionaries — SAOL's and SO's own inflection index confirming grepar as the plural of grep. So this fix rests on the authority after all, not on a cross-check source. sv.wiktionary independently agrees (grep/grepen/grepar/greparna, 'grep u', glossed '(jordbruk) ett gaffelformigt redskap för jordbruk och trädgårdsskötsel'). The stored zero plural is the ett-word pattern applied to an en-word. I opened tools bw/garden_fork@2x.webp: a three-tine fork with a slim tapered handle and a hang hole — the first round's hedge about the tines being slenderer than a real grep's is a fair lemma note, but it does not touch this form fix.

SAOL 'gecko [gek´o] substantiv ~n ~r'; SO 'gecko geckon geckor'. Both agree; the stored 'Geckos' is an imported English plural in neither authority. The proposal's own reasoning is the right one and I tested it: the -s ending is not uniformly wrong for loans (SAOL gives kettlebell '~s' and bagel '~s' in this same batch), so it genuinely has to be looked up word by word — which is exactly the discipline that makes the keyboard REJECT below possible.

SAOL 'hemlock [hem´låk] substantiv ~en ~ar / ett barrträd'; SO 'hemlock hemlocken hemlockar'. Both agree. The stored zero plural would require an ett-word; hemlock is ~en, and the row's own gender 'n' is the field that is right. ART NOTE (held elsewhere, does not affect the form): SAOL defines hemlock as a CONIFER ('ett barrträd') while the art is a broadleaf deciduous tree — a cross-locale art question, not a Swedish form defect.

THE FIX IS DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT BUT MUST NOT SHIP AS WRITTEN — my rule-7 dup scan caught the one thing the first round did not. 'Sjukhuskläderar' is indefensible (the -ar default bolted onto an already-plural noun; SAOB: 'KLÄDER, pl., se KLÄDE'), so it cannot stay. But patching the plural to 'Sjukhuskläder' makes this row ['Sjukhuskläder','Sjukhuskläder','n'] BYTE-IDENTICAL to the sister key 'scrubs' — the ONLY new collision my scan found across all 39 patched keys, and one CREATED by the fix rather than pre-existing. The two keys are different garments: scrubs is what STAFF wear (de OP-Kleidung, es Uniforme médico, nl Operatiekleding) and a hospital gown is what the PATIENT wears. The cross-locale test makes this decisive: ALL 10 other locales give hospital-gown a COUNTABLE singular patient garment with a real plural (de Krankenhaushemd/Krankenhaushemden, fr Blouse d'hôpital/Blouses d'hôpital, es Bata de hospital/Batas, it Camice ospedaliero/Camici, nl Ziekenhuisjas/Ziekenhuisjassen, da Hospitalskittel/Hospitalskitler, no Sykehuskjole/Sykehuskjoler, fi Sairaalatakki/Sairaalatakit) — Swedish ALONE has collapsed a patient gown into plural-only 'hospital clothes', which is precisely why the script had nothing to pluralise. AND the proposal's stated ground is false: 'Removing the invented form is right whichever way the lemma question is settled' does NOT hold — if the lemma resolves to Patientrock the plural is Patientrockar, not Sjukhuskläder, so this fix is not lemma-independent and would entrench the defect behind a duplicate. Operator must rule the lemma (recommend Patientrock/Patientrockar/n, which also resolves the separately-held gender row, since a plural-only noun can carry neither en nor ett). Delete the non-word — but do not ship a byte-identical twin of scrubs.

NO PLURAL IS ATTESTED ANYWHERE, AND THE PROPOSAL'S ANALOGUE IS THE WRONG CLASS. Verified verbatim: 'Inga träffar på iguanodon' in SAOL, SO and SAOB alike — quoted honestly by the proposal. I then went one step further and checked the source the proposal did not cite: sv.wiktionary DOES have an iguanodon entry, but it carries only 'iguanodon u' with NO Böjningar table at all — so the gender (utrum, = the stored n) is corroborated while the plural is attested by nothing, in any source. That leaves the proposed 'Iguanodoner' resting entirely on the cited elektron pattern — and that analogue does not hold: elektron/proton/neutron are -tron/-on words, whereas iguanodon is a Greek -ODON word (sv.wiktionary etymology: 'grekiska ὀδών (odṓn)'). SAOL's actual -odon control is 'mast·odont [-odån´t] substantiv ~en ~er' — Swedish nativises Greek -odon by taking the oblique stem odont- and adding a -T, giving mastodont -> mastodonter. That points at a LEMMA question (Iguanodont -> iguanodonter?), which per the brief is reserved to the operator and is more than a form correction. Both the stored -ar (the script's unmotivated default; the Latin -us rule cannot reach a Greek stem) and the proposed -er are unattested guesses, so this is not 'keep the stored value' — it is 'neither form is sourced; rule it explicitly'. The proposal itself invites exactly this ('Operator may prefer to leave it pending a native/palaeontology-usage check'), and I agree: do not ship an invented plural to children on a pattern argument built from the wrong word class.

SAOL 'sylt substantiv ~en ~er'; SO 'sylt sylten sylter'. Both give a real plural outright, and classification independently says countable-thing/hasPlural:true, so the identical singular/plural wrongly encodes 'no plural'. This is the brief's named inverse trap (bread/asparagus/cheese) and the dictionary wins. Noted: sylter is 'kinds of jam' and is adult register beside a picture of one jar — but SAOL is explicit and the brief is explicit that the dictionary governs.
SAOL 'juice [jo´s] substantiv ~n [jo´sen]; pl. ~r [jo`ser]'; SO 'juice juicen juicer'. Both give the plural outright. Treating juice as uncountable is an English intuition SAOL does not share.

SAOL 'kettle|bell [ket´elbel] substantiv ~en; pl. ~s' — SAOL gives ONLY -s. SO has no entry ('Inga träffar på kettlebell'), so there is no competing authority and this is NOT a rule-5 conflict. 'Kettlebellar' is the -ar default. I specifically re-read SO here because the neighbouring keyboard proposal turns on SO — SO's silence on kettlebell is what makes these two words diverge legitimately.

REJECT — THE PROPOSAL WOULD REPLACE A CORRECT, AUTHORITY-SANCTIONED FORM, AND ITS CENTRAL FACTUAL CLAIM IS FALSE. The proposal asserts SAOL 'does NOT list *keyboards' and concludes the stored 'Keyboards' is a script artifact to be replaced by 'Keyboardar'. It consulted SAOL only. I fetched BOTH authorities and re-verified twice: SO reads 'keyboard keyboarden el. keyboardet, plural KEYBOARDS äv. keyboardar' — SO lists KEYBOARDS FIRST, as its primary plural. So the stored value is not invented and is not wrong; it is SO's first-listed form, and the proposal's own first-listed policy (which it invokes by name: 'Taking SAOL's first-listed form') would endorse it under SO. What is actually here is the brief's rule-5 class exactly: SAOL ('pl. ~ar el. ~' — keyboardar or zero, no -s) and SO ('keyboards äv. keyboardar') GENUINELY DISAGREE, like bison/mango/frisbee. Per the brief that is 'a finding to FLAG, not something to resolve by picking' — and the proposal picked, silently, without disclosing that the other authority contradicts it. Destroying a correct form is the worst outcome available here. LEAVE 'Keyboards' STANDING and surface the SAOL/SO conflict to the operator. (Note the row's gender 't' is also sanctioned — SAOL '~en el. ~et' — so no consequential change follows.)

SAOL 'lav·endel [-en´del] substantiv ~n' — no plural listed; SO 'lavendel lavendeln' — no plural listed. Both silent, and SAOL demonstrably does list plurals when they exist (kornell ~en ~er, hemlock ~en ~ar in this same batch), so the omission is meaningful. Contradicts classification hasPlural:true and the dictionary wins. Cross-locale corroboration: de already ships Lavendel/Lavendel (zero), so sv is not made an outlier. The proposal is also fair that 'Lavendlar' is at least well-formed syncope — but no authority sanctions it.

SAOL 'lime [laj´m] substantiv ~n [-en]; pl. ~r [-er]'; SO 'lime limen limer'. Both agree. lime ends in unstressed -e -> 2nd declension -r. Note the row has two diverging themes (fruits = the fruit, colors = a colour swatch); classification fixed countable-thing, which the fruit art supports, so the form fix is safe.

CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED. Class rule verified at the attested member: SAOL 'kakt·us [kak´t-] substantiv ~en ~ar'. Parasaurolophus DOES end in Latin -us (Greek λόφος -> Latinised -lophus), so the -us -> -ar rule genuinely reaches it — this is not the overreach the brief warns about with carnotaurus. I also enumerated the whole corpus rather than trusting the proposal's two cited siblings: of the 19 Latin -us dinosaur keys, EIGHTEEN already take -ar (Allosaurusar, Ankylosaurusar, Apatosaurusar, Argentinosaurusar, Brachiosaurusar, Brontosaurusar, Giganotosaurusar, Ichthyosaurusar, Mosasaurusar, Pachycephalosaurusar, Plesiosaurusar, Stegosaurusar — which the brief itself blesses as correct — Styracosaurusar, Therizinosaurusar, and others); parasaurolophus is the LONE zero-plural outlier. Pure form correction.

SAOL 'pegas [pega´s] substantiv ~en ~er'; SO 'pegas pegasen pegaser'. Both agree. The stored zero plural is wrong under either lemma. Moves coherently with the singular fix (rule 7): the row becomes Pegas/Pegaser/n, one consistent lemma; dup scan clean.
SAOL 'persimon [-må´n] substantiv ~en ~er'; SO 'persimon persimonen persimoner'. Both agree. The -ar default swallowing the 3rd declension again.

SAOL 'flox [flåk´s] substantiv ~en' — gender only, no plural; SO 'flox floxen' — singular and definite singular only. Both silent, so 'Floxar' is unattested. The proposal's refusal to invent a replacement plural is exactly right and is the discipline this commission exists to enforce. Cross-locale corroboration the proposal did not cite: fr, es and it ALREADY ship a zero plural for this key (Phlox/Phlox, Flox/Flox), so sv is not made an outlier. NAIVE-REPAIR TRAP CHECKED: 'Flox' must NOT be 'repaired' toward any å/ä/ö form — it carries no diacritic and none is expected.

SAOL 'pick|up [-ap´] substantiv ~en ~er' with sense 2 'liten lastbil' — exactly this key; SO 'pickup pickupen pickuper'. BOTH authorities agree on -er, so this is not a rule-5 conflict. The proposal is right that this cuts against the batch-01 'EN loans take -s' heuristic and that the dictionary wins — and the wider set proves the point: SAOL gives -s for kettlebell and bagel, -er for pickup, -r for gecko and lime, and -ar for suv. There is no loan class rule; each was looked up.

Homograph handled correctly, verified verbatim: SAOL '1squash substantiv ~en / ett racketspel' (the GAME, no plural) and '2squash substantiv ~en ~er / en pumpa'; SO likewise '1 squash squashen' vs '2 squash squashen squasher / typ av gurkliknande pumpa'. The art is a pear-shaped winter squash, i.e. sense 2 -> squasher. Both authorities agree on the vegetable sense. Resolves the v1 HOLD correctly.

SAOL 'suv [su´v el. suv´] substantiv ~en ~ar' — plain tildes, NO colon; SO 'suv suven suvar'. Both agree. The proposal's reasoning is sound and I verified the contrast it rests on: SAOL DOES write colons when it means them (tv '~:n ~:ar') but writes suv and ufo as ordinary lexicalised words, so the per-word entry overrides a blanket initialism rule, and the colon is additionally a TTS hazard on a site that reads words aloud. ROW-COHERENCE NOTE for the operator (rule 7, not an objection — the 'to' value itself is correct): the fix leaves the singular untouched, so the row becomes 'SUV'/'Suvar' — before the fix it was consistently all-caps (SUV/SUV:ar), so the fix CREATES a casing mismatch inside the row. SAOL lemmatises lowercase 'suv'. Recommend the operator also take the singular to 'Suv'. Identical situation at ufo.

SAOL 'tejp substantiv ~en ~er' sense 1 'självhäftande klisterremsa'; SO 'tejp tejpen tejper'. Both agree, and sense 1 matches the art (a roll of adhesive tape). Stored zero plural unsupported; classification hasPlural:true agrees.

Verified: SAOL 'taxi [tak´si] substantiv ~n, i pl. används vanl. taxibilar'; SO 'taxi taxin; som plural kan användas taxibilar'. BOTH authorities decline an inflected plural of taxi and BOTH name taxibilar, so 'Taxier' is unsupported. ROW-COHERENCE TENSION, surfaced because it is a real one: the plural field will hold a DIFFERENT LEMMA (taxibil) from the singular (taxi) — structurally the same shape the first round HELD lego and domino for ('the row silently switches word between its own singular and plural fields'). I judge it defensible HERE, and the distinction is principled: SAOL prescribes taxibilar AS the plural of taxi INSIDE the taxi entry itself (authority-sanctioned suppletion), whereas Legobitar is a script artifact SAOL never sanctions for lego. The operator should know that marking taxi NO_PLURAL is the equally defensible alternative, since neither dictionary inflects taxi itself.

SAOL 'timer [taj´mer] substantiv ~n; pl. ~' — zero plural; SO 'timer timern, plural timer'. Both agree. 'Timrar' misapplies -el/-er syncope (nyckel->nycklar, hummer->humrar) to an English loan neither authority syncopates — a manufactured non-word of the Gardinerar/Musklerar class. Cross-locale corroboration: de and it already ship Timer/Timer (zero). CAVEAT on the proposal's framing: 'Independent of the singular HOLD: whatever the lemma, Timrar is not a Swedish form' is true in its second half but loose in its first — the art is a twin-bell wind-up ALARM CLOCK showing a time of day (väckarklocka), and if the lemma moves there the plural becomes väckarklockor, not Timer. The fix is correct ON THE CURRENT LEMMA, which is the right scope for a form correction; it simply is not lemma-independent.

CONFIRMED WITH THE CONFIDENCE CAVEAT PRESERVED. Citation verified verbatim, including the negative: SAOL/SO/SAOB all return 'Inga träffar på triceratops. Menade du triceps eller triumfator?' — stated honestly, not fabricated. sv.wiktionary carries an explicit utrum paradigm: triceratops / triceratopsen / TRICERATOPSER / triceratopserna. The stored 'Triceratopsar' presupposes the Latin -us -> -ar rule, and I confirm that rule cannot reach this word: triceratops ends in Greek -ops (ὤψ), not Latin -us, so the -ar has no licence — whereas -er is both the attested paradigm and the regular outcome for utrum consonant-final learned loans. WHY I CONFIRM THIS BUT ESCALATE IGUANODON (the principled line): triceratops HAS an attested paradigm in a lexicographic source; iguanodon's sv.wiktionary entry has NO Böjningar table at all, so its proposed plural is sourced by nothing. One edition is thin evidence and the proposal says so itself and asks for a second native opinion — I am it, and I judge that an attested paradigm plus a correct class analysis beats an unsourced default whose only rule is demonstrably inapplicable.

SAOL 'ufo [u´fo] substantiv ~t ~n' — plain tildes, NO colon; SO 'ufo ufot ufon'. Both agree, and ~t confirms the stored gender t, so the row stays coherent. The tv contrast ('tv ~:n ~:ar' WITH colons) is real and I verified it is SAOL's own per-word choice. SAOB records historical variety (pl. -n, äv. -s l. = l. -r) but SAOL and SO both settle on -n, and SAOL is the norm. ROW-COHERENCE NOTE (same as suv, not an objection): the fix leaves the singular as 'UFO', so the row becomes 'UFO'/'Ufon' — a casing mismatch the fix creates. SAOL lemmatises lowercase 'ufo'. Recommend the operator also take the singular to 'Ufo'.

THE HOMOGRAPH SPLIT IS REAL AND I VERIFIED IT VERBATIM RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE QUOTE — this is the 1trapets/2trapets inverse trap the brief names, and the proposal reads it the right way round. SAOL: '1trapets [trapet´s] substantiv ~en ~er / ett gymnastikredskap' and '2trapets [trapet´s] substantiv ~et ~er / parallelltrapets'. SO is even more explicit: '2 trapets trapetset trapetser / ⟨geometri, matematik⟩ fyrhörning med två parallella men olika långa sidor'. I OPENED shapes/trapezoid@2x.webp myself: a bare pale-green quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides, black outline, no other content — SO's definition word for word, i.e. sense 2 -> ~et -> ETT-ord -> t. Gender-code direction double-checked per the brief's warning: t = ETT-ord = neuter, so 'ett trapets' is what this fix produces, which is correct; the stored 'n' would read the maths shape aloud as a circus apparatus.
